meta.title.data-collection: Data Collection: gathering a client's documents, from 0 to 100% | Case study by Hugo Ferrer
meta.desc.data-collection: Case study: discovery and design of document collection for an HR and finance consulting firm. Eight interviews, a synthesis run with AI and verified by hand, eight decisions, one journey from 0 to 100%.

dc.hero.lede: Discovery, then design, of document collection for an HR and finance consulting firm: eight interviews, a synthesis run with AI and verified by hand, and one principle, seeing what is missing the moment a file arrives.

dc.s1.title: The problem: four sticking points, always the same
dc.s1.intro: Every engagement at the firm starts with the same step: getting the client's documents, sometimes covering three years and hundreds of sites. This collection ran on emails, a file-sharing space and spreadsheets.
dc.s1.k1.d: Endless back-and-forth with the client, and no signal when a file is uploaded.
dc.s1.k1.q: “A few days go by between the moment they upload the docs and the moment we notice.”
dc.s1.k2.d: No way to know whether a case file is complete without opening the files one by one.
dc.s1.k2.q: “Sometimes the thing is called 2025, you open it, and it's 2024.”
dc.s1.k3.d: Converting, cleaning and normalising payroll data, with up to a thousand payroll items to classify by hand for a single case.
dc.s1.k3.q: “It can happen that we hit refresh and wait three hours.”
dc.s1.k4.d: Each new year, the same collection starts again for ongoing cases and ties up the teams for months.

dc.s1.take: Before designing anything: name the sticking points, and measure what they cost.
dc.s2.title: The field study: eight interviews, four areas of expertise
dc.s2.intro: In July 2026, I interviewed the people who live through the collection: consultants, payroll experts, managers, an operations lead, a business developer. Each interview was recorded, then completed by watching real case files on screen. The area most advanced on the subject served as the pilot.
dc.s2.panel.caption: One square per person interviewed. The areas of expertise are not named.
dc.s2.corpus.title: The corpus
dc.s2.corpus.3: Real case files, opened on screen with the consultants.
dc.s2.st1.d: Eight recorded interviews, and real case files opened on screen.
dc.s2.st2.d: Every step of the collection, from signature to report.
dc.s2.st3.d: One main persona: the consultant who runs the collection.
dc.s2.st4.d: A matrix: each difficulty tied to a possible solution.
dc.s2.take: Five interviews in one area, three elsewhere: enough to see what repeats, and what belongs to a single trade.
dc.s3.title: AI gathers, I verify
dc.s3.intro: Eight interviews mean hours of recordings. I handed AI what it does fast, and kept what carries responsibility. In tax advisory and cost optimisation, the know-how is complex and every lever matters: a plausible answer is not enough. So every output was reread, corrected and reframed, point by point.
dc.s3.p1.ai: Each recorded interview is transcribed and summarised automatically.
dc.s3.p1.me: I run the interview, over real case files opened on screen.
dc.s3.p2.ai: An AI notebook answers only from the transcripts and documents, and cites every passage.
dc.s3.p2.me: I ask the questions, analyse each output and reframe it.
dc.s3.p3.ai: It groups the quotes, suggests frequencies, links pain points to leads.
dc.s3.p3.me: I recount interview by interview and reread each quote in its transcript.
dc.s3.p4.ai: It produces the screens and the test prototype.
dc.s3.p4.me: I set the journeys, the copy and the edge cases, then audit the consistency.
dc.s3.say: The same rule as for the product: the tool alerts, the human decides.
dc.s3.g1.d: Every quote kept is reread in its original transcript.
dc.s3.g2.d: Every “5 of 5” is checked interview by interview.
dc.s3.g3.d: Findings are tested against case files opened on screen.
dc.s3.g4.d: Findings and decisions are presented to the manager and the product manager.
dc.s3.f.title: What the interviews established
dc.s3.f.legend: Frequency observed across the five interviews of the pilot area. Each finding keeps its quotes.
dc.s3.f1: Collection is a game of ping-pong, with no signal when a file arrives.
dc.s3.f2: Reprocessing the data is the biggest time sink: every payroll software has its own layout.
dc.s3.f2.q1: “The biggest job is going to be cleaning up that data.”
dc.s3.f3: An incomplete case file does not show on arrival: it is discovered in the middle of the analysis.
dc.s3.f3.q2: “Miss one month and everything is wrong.”
dc.s3.f4: The DSN, the payroll return French employers file every month, is the only standardised data: the one everyone trusts.
dc.s3.f4.q1: “Green, I have the DSN. Red, I don't.”
dc.s3.f5: The tool should raise alerts, never decide in the consultant's place.
dc.s3.f5.q1: “We stop digging, and we lose the expertise.”
dc.s3.f5.c1: A senior consultant, about a fully automated audit
dc.s3.f6: Tracking is declarative: nothing keeps a trace of what has been checked.
dc.s3.f6.q1: “There's no real trace of everything I've checked.”
dc.s3.f6.q2: “As soon as they move to Excel, it goes off into another world. You lose all visibility.”
dc.s3.f7: Four areas of expertise, four ways of working: the same document can be requested several times from the same client.
dc.s3.take: AI speeds up the sifting. It signs off on no finding: each one was verified, one by one.
dc.s4.title: Eight decisions, and what they rule out
dc.s4.intro: Each decision answers a finding and, most of the time, says what it refuses. Two decisions frame the work, six shape the product.
dc.s4.c7: Four areas, four ways of working
dc.s4.d3.t: See what is missing the moment a file arrives
dc.s4.d6.t: Client side: a list and a guided upload
dc.s4.d7.t: The tool alerts, the consultant decides
dc.s4.flow.caption: From finding to decision: hover a line to follow the thread.
dc.s4.frame.title: Two decisions to frame the work
dc.s4.frame.legend: Before the screens: narrow the scope so it can ship.
dc.s4.d1.d: Collection on one side, data reliability on the other: two scopes, two delivery rhythms. To the neighbouring workstream, one requirement passed on: one template per payroll software.
dc.s4.d1.out: The single project that mixes collection and anomaly detection.
dc.s4.d2.d: The area where the stakes are highest and the process most mature serves as the testing ground. The other three provide the counterpoint.
dc.s4.d2.out: Launching the tool in every area at the same time.
dc.s4.design.title: Six decisions to design the product
dc.s4.design.legend: You will find them again, marker by marker, in the journey that follows.
dc.s4.d3.d: Every upload is checked on arrival: right format, right period, missing months. A view by site and by month shows the gaps at a glance.
dc.s4.d3.from: Invisible incompleteness, and the DSN as the reference
dc.s4.d3.out: Opening the files one by one to check.
dc.s4.d4.d: No status to fill in by hand: every state of the case file follows from a real action.
dc.s4.d4.out: A tracking tool that has to be filled in. The previous one had been abandoned, too slow to keep up to date.
dc.s4.d5.d: A core set of documents without which no case can start, and a standard collection pack.
dc.s4.d5.out: The exhaustive questionnaire sent to the client.
dc.s4.d6.d: The client needs a clear instruction, not a project management tool. The file itself says where it belongs: the site and the month are read at every upload.
dc.s4.d6.out: The full portal with a dashboard: a client would rather pick up the phone.
dc.s4.d7.d: A rejected file shows its reason in plain words and the action expected. The analysis itself stays in the experts' hands.
dc.s4.d7.out: The fully automated audit, a black box that would smooth over the anomalies only they know how to spot.
dc.s4.d8.d: The reminder only covers documents still expected: complete items are not requested again. Automatic reminders stop for each complete, validated set.
dc.s4.voc.title: A shared vocabulary
dc.s4.voc.legend: Four areas of expertise, four ways of naming document tracking. The design settles on a few terms.
dc.s4.voc1.d: The list of requested documents, with statuses and deadlines.
dc.s4.voc2.d: What a case cannot start without.
dc.s4.voc3.d: The grid of sites, month by month.
dc.s4.voc4.d: The client: they upload, they do not run a project.
dc.s4.take: Saying no is part of design: seven decisions out of eight name what they rule out.
dc.s5.title: The journey, from 0 to 100%
dc.s5.intro: Four journeys cross in a single loop. Here are eight steps of it, on the consultant's side and the client's side. On each screen, a marker says what the interface does, and which decision it comes from.
dc.s5.loop1.d: Create the client, prepare and send the initial request.
dc.s5.loop2.d: Receive the request, upload, fix or sort the files.
dc.s5.loop3.d: Find the client to assign, apply, then save.
dc.s5.loop4.d: Review the files, upload on the client's behalf and prepare a reminder.
dc.s5.loop5.d: Receive a reminder, and requests for further documents.
dc.s5.st1.d: The list of 26 document types is sent to the client. Nothing is complete yet: everything reads “To upload”.
dc.shot.aria: Mockup excerpt, scrollable sideways on small screens
dc.s5.st1.alt: Mockup excerpt, interface in French: the “Upload on the client's behalf” area, then the list of the 26 requested document types, all marked “To upload”.
dc.s5.h11.d: Files received by email enter the same circuit: same check, same tracking.
dc.s5.h12.d: “To upload”, “To complete”, “Complete”: each state follows from a real upload.
dc.s5.st2.d: Fourteen files uploaded: nine accepted, five rejected. The client knows right away, without waiting for the firm to get back to them.
dc.s5.st2.alt: Mockup excerpt, interface in French: a banner reading “Check complete, 14 DSN files, 9 accepted, 5 rejected”, then the “What is still missing” card.
dc.s5.h21.d: Format, period, site: what passes is kept, what blocks is flagged at once.
dc.s5.h22.d: Three lines: what is missing, and the button to act.
dc.s5.st3.d: Each rejection shows its reason and what to do. Nobody needs to call to understand.
dc.s5.st3.alt: Mockup excerpt, interface in French: the DSN upload area, then five rejected files, each with its reason and a button to upload it again.
dc.s5.h31.t: The file says where it belongs
dc.s5.h31.d: The site number (SIRET) and the month are read from each file: nothing to fill in.
dc.s5.h32.d: “Unreadable period: export this file again from your payroll software.” The rejection explains, and guides.
dc.s5.st4.d: As uploads come in, the list empties. It only shows the documents and periods still missing.
dc.s5.st4.alt: Mockup excerpt, client side, interface in French: 23 types complete, and the “What is still missing” card with three types to complete.
dc.s5.h41.d: Checked uploads disappear from the list: the client does not reread what they have already provided.
dc.s5.h42.d: Each site has its own periods: what is missing is counted per site, not per case.
dc.s5.st5.t: The same state, seen from the firm
dc.s5.st5.d: The consultant sees exactly what the client sees. They can upload on the client's behalf, or send a reminder.
dc.s5.st5.alt: Mockup excerpt, consultant side, interface in French: collection tracking, the “Chase what is missing” and “Refresh” buttons, and the same “What is still missing” card.
dc.s5.h51.t: Chase from here, in one move
dc.s5.h51.d: The reminder starts from the tracking screen, already limited to what is missing.
dc.s5.h52.d: Client and consultant read the same state: no more back-and-forth to know where the case stands.
dc.s5.st6.d: One row per site, one cell per month, across the whole period to cover. The gaps show without opening a single file.
dc.s5.st6.alt: Mockup excerpt, interface in French: the DSN grid, one row per site, one cell per month from 2023 to 2026.
dc.s5.k.c4: Finding · The DSN is the reference
dc.s5.h61.t: One cell, one month, one site
dc.s5.h61.d: “Green, I have the DSN. Red, I don't.” A payroll expert's sentence became the screen.
dc.s5.h62.t: Missing is not out of period
dc.s5.h62.d: A site that opens or closes during the year has no gap: the grid tells the two apart.
dc.s5.st7.t: Chase, but only what is missing
dc.s5.st7.d: The reminder dialog only ticks the documents still expected, with their periods. Reminders stop by themselves for each complete set.
dc.s5.st7.alt: Excerpt from the reminder dialog, interface in French: only the three documents still to be provided are ticked.
dc.s5.h71.t: Only what is missing is ticked
dc.s5.h71.d: Complete items are not requested again.
dc.s5.h72.d: The reminder specifies the months expected, not just the document's name.
dc.s5.st8.d: 26 types out of 26: the scope is covered and the files are valid. Reminders stop, the analysis begins.
dc.s5.st8.alt: Mockup excerpt, interface in French: a banner reading “26 types complete”, reminders stopped, and the list where every type is “Complete”.
dc.s5.h81.d: Scope covered, files valid: reminders stop without anyone having to think about it.
dc.s5.h82.d: No status was filled in by hand between the request and the complete case file.

dc.s5.edge.title: Three edge cases that weighed in
dc.s5.edge.legend: They come from the interviews, not from a textbook list.
dc.s5.e1.d: A single absent month skews the year's calculations: the per-site view flags it on upload.
dc.s5.e2.d: Wrongly named or in the wrong format, it is checked on arrival and rejected with its reason.
dc.s5.e3.d: Hundreds of sites open and close: the grid tells a missing month from a month out of period.
dc.s5.take: Every screen carries at least one decision: nothing is there for decoration.

dc.s6.aud.title: An audit before acceptance testing
dc.s6.aud.d: I reread the four journeys as a single story and listed the inconsistencies: copy that does not match the state on screen, reference figures that differ from one screen to the next, duplicate naming, gaps in the journey.
dc.s6.aud.cases: Eight edge cases to replay in the prototype
dc.s6.quick: One gain proposed without a line of development: switch on the upload alert of the file-sharing space already in place.
dc.s6.num.title: What about the numbers?
dc.s6.num.d: There are no post-launch figures yet, and I will not make any up. Discovery showed that collection time was not measured anywhere: the design therefore timestamps each step (request, upload, complete case file), to have a baseline for comparison.
dc.s6.hand.title: The handoff
dc.s6.hand.d: The development team praised the journeys for their precision and technical clarity.
dc.s6.learn.title: What I take away
dc.s6.l1: A payslip cannot be read like a generic document: every payroll software has its own layout, so each one needs its own template.
dc.s6.l2: A tracking tool that asks people to enter statuses by hand ends up abandoned.
dc.s6.l3: The client does not want to follow a project online: they want a clear upload instruction.
dc.s6.l4: Automation, AI included, should surface alerts and leave the investigation to the experts.
dc.end.title: A business tool to make readable?
